name: Evolving Workflows
summary: Evolving Workflows turns work your agents repeat into reviewed, versioned workflows that a Bound agent runs on a schedule.
description: Agents suggest a workflow when they repeat work, with evidence. Evolving Workflows also spots repeated done issues in Task Board. You review each suggestion, edit a draft (steps, allowed operations, trigger), promote it to a versioned workflow, export a recipe that creates a Bound agent in Portal, and schedule it. The Bound agent’s own runner claims each due run at most once; every run is a Task Board issue assigned to that agent. A Bound agent may call only the allowed operations; it is not forced to follow the steps.

intents: make a bound agent for a routine

operations.title: Suggest a workflow
operations.description: Suggest that repeated work becomes a reviewed workflow. Give a title, the evidence (Task Board issue ids or receipt call ids of the work you repeated) and, if you can, the steps you took and the operations each step used. The owner reviews every suggestion; nothing runs automatically.

operations.title: List my suggestions
operations.description: List the suggestions you made (newest first) with their review status.

operations.title: Get a suggestion
operations.description: Read one of your suggestions with its evidence, steps and the owner's decision.

operations.title: Get a workflow
operations.description: Read a promoted workflow: instruction, trigger, reviewed steps and the operations you may call. A Bound agent reads its workflow here before it works; for a Free agent the notice says that it runs with its own access and the operation list is guidance. Without version: the active version.

operations.title: Due workflow runs
operations.description: For a Bound or a Free agent: the scheduled runs due now on the schedules that name you and target your own mode (a Bound agent gets Bound schedules, a Free agent gets Free ones). A paused or removed agent gets none. Reading claims nothing (it only records runs whose due time passed the misfire grace as missed); claim a run with routine_claim before you start it. Your `tealbrick agent serve` routines mode calls this for you. A schedule that moved to the engine gives nothing here: use steps_due. Deprecated; it stays for one release for Bound agents.

operations.title: Claim a due run
operations.description: Claim one due run by its occurrence. At most one claim per occurrence ever succeeds; a run that was claimed, missed or is not due answers claimed false with a reason. You can claim only an occurrence of your own schedule of your own mode: mode_mismatch (the schedule targets the other mode), agent_unavailable (you are paused or removed), not_bound (not an agent, or a Free agent with no Free schedule). The answer carries the reviewed workflow (instruction, steps, allowed operations). migrated: the schedule moved to the engine (C367 M3); its agent takes the work as workflow steps (steps_due, step_claim, step_report). This path is deprecated and stays for one release.

operations.title: Report a run
operations.description: Report the state of a run you claimed: dispatched (the turn started), then completed, failed or uncertain, with a short summary. Repeating the same report changes nothing. With the report that ends the run (completed or failed) you may send metrics (the RunReport: ok, minutes, retries, questions_to_martin, lessons, and metrics: your own named numbers, name to number, at most 20). They are stored once with that report; the owner sees them per workflow version, no agent sees them. metrics.pipeline, metrics.version and metrics.issue are optional and ignored. Metrics on any other status are refused (metrics_need_terminal_status). If the workflow version was imported from a pipeline contract, a named metric must be declared there (metric_not_declared). If a report with metrics is refused, send it again without metrics, so the run still ends.

metrics.description: Per-pipeline numbers: name to number (from -1e12 to 1e12). A name starts with a lower case letter and has 2 to 41 characters (lower case letters, digits, underscore). At most 20 per report, and at most 20 different names per workflow version. Omit a metric you could not measure.

issue.description: Task Board issue id of the run. Accepted and ignored: the run itself says which issue it has.

operations.title: Workflow steps offered to you
operations.description: For a Free agent: the steps of running workflows that are offered to you now, each as {stepRunId, workflowTitle, deadline}. An agent step asks you for content, not for an action. A Bound agent, a paused agent and a removed agent get none. Reading claims nothing; claim a step with step_claim before you work on it. Your `tealbrick agent serve` steps mode calls this for you.

operations.title: Claim a workflow step
operations.description: Claim one offered step by its stepRunId. At most one agent ever claims a step attempt, once; the same agent asking again for a step it claimed (its answer was lost) gets the same answer again, as a read that changes nothing; a step that is claimed, ended, timed out, cancelled, not yours or not for your mode answers claimed false with a reason (already_claimed, finished, timed_out, cancelled, not_found, mode_mismatch, agent_unavailable). The answer carries the instruction, the typed inputs, the outputSchema your answer must match, an allowedHint (guidance only: you act with your own access), the deadline and heartbeatSec. It says mode content: return the output only, do not act. The step is not a task to carry out; the engine runs every action itself. The claim takes no idempotency key on purpose: the SDK would keep a copy of the answer, and the inputs can hold data of other apps. That is why a lost answer is safe to ask again.

inputs.description: The typed inputs of the step: name to value.

outputSchema.description: A JSON Schema (type object). Your output must match it.

operations.title: Keep a claimed step alive
operations.description: Tell the engine that you still work on a step you claimed. Send it at least every heartbeatSec seconds (heartbeatSec 0 means the workflow asks for no heartbeat; then only the deadline applies): after three missed heartbeats, or after the deadline, the step times out and you get a refusal (step_timed_out) here and on step_report. A step the engine cancelled answers step_cancelled. Stop working when you get a refusal.

operations.title: Report a workflow step
operations.description: Report the end of a step you claimed: completed with the typed output, or failed with a short summary. The output is checked against the outputSchema of the step: an output that does not match answers 422 output_invalid with a pointer to the field, and the step stays claimed until it times out, so you can report again. Repeating a report that already ended the step changes nothing. With the report you may send a summary (at most 500 characters, the owner sees it) and metrics (your own named numbers, name to number, at most 20; the owner sees them, no agent does). Return the output only: do not act.

output.description: The typed output. Required with completed.

metrics.description: Named numbers: name to number (from -1e12 to 1e12). A name starts with a lower case letter and has 2 to 41 characters (lower case letters, digits, underscore). At most 20.

operations.title: Agent steps
operations.description: The agent steps of workflow runs, newest first: which agent card was offered the step, who claimed it, heartbeats, timeouts, cancellations and re-offers (attempts), the size of the output, and the summary and numbers the agent reported. Of one run, of one workflow, or of all. Never the inputs and never the output itself. Owner only.

operations.title: Move from 0.3.x
operations.description: What the one-time move of 0.3.x workflows to the engine did: how many workflows and schedules moved, how many stayed on the 0.3.x runner because their agent is Bound (legacy_bound), how many were skipped or failed and why, and what waits for the engine (deferred). Each item names the engine workflow or schedule it became. Owner only.

operations.title: Suggestions to review
operations.description: All suggestions in this workspace, newest first.

operations.title: Suggestion detail
operations.description: One suggestion with its history and the drafts made from it.

operations.title: Decide a suggestion
operations.description: Approve, reject or archive a suggestion.

operations.title: Scan Task Board for repeated work
operations.description: Read done Task Board issues now and suggest work one agent repeated at least minRepeats times. Evolving Workflows also does this in the background every 15 minutes. It reads only the projects you share with Evolving Workflows in Task Board.

operations.title: Task Board scan status
operations.description: When Evolving Workflows last read Task Board for repeated work (in the background every 15 minutes, or when you scan), and what it found.

operations.title: Workflow templates
operations.description: Seed workflow templates the owner can start a draft from.

operations.title: Create a draft
operations.description: Create a workflow draft from an approved suggestion, from a template, or empty.

operations.title: Drafts
operations.description: All workflow drafts, newest first.

operations.title: Draft detail
operations.description: One workflow draft. `pipeline` says which pipeline contract it was imported from (null for a draft that was not imported).

operations.title: Edit a draft
operations.description: Change a draft's text, steps or allowed operations. Send the revision you edited; a stale revision is refused.

operations.title: Promote a draft
operations.description: Make the reviewed draft a permanent workflow version (version 1, or the next version of its workflow).

operations.title: Import a pipeline contract
operations.description: Import a typed pipeline contract (tealbrick.agents/pipeline-contract/0.1) as a new workflow draft. Teal Brick tools of the steps become the step operations and the allowed operations; every other tool is listed as not mapped; the rest of the contract is kept as data and is not enforced. No schedule is created: the report gives the trigger as a hint. With asDraftOf the draft is a new draft of that workflow. Agents that run the workflow read its title, summary and step text; everything else of the contract stays with the owner.

asDraftOf.description: A workflow that was imported from the same pipeline id (or never imported): the draft becomes its next version when promoted.

confirmReplace.description: Needed with asDraftOf when the workflow was never imported from a contract: the draft replaces its steps and allowed operations.

operations.title: Export a pipeline contract
operations.description: A pipeline contract (tealbrick.agents/pipeline-contract/0.1) rebuilt from one version of a workflow. A workflow imported from a contract gives that contract back, except the fields Evolution owns (status, and the purpose, steps and Teal Brick tools you edited). A workflow that was never imported gets documented defaults for the required fields.

omitted.description: Allowed operations (product.operation) that no step uses: a contract lists tools per step, so they are not in it.

operations.title: Workflows
operations.description: All permanent workflows.

operations.title: Workflow versions
operations.description: Every version of one workflow, oldest first. `pipelines` lists the versions that came from an imported pipeline contract.

operations.title: Compare versions
operations.description: What changed between two versions of a workflow: text, steps and allowed operations.

operations.title: Export a Bound-agent recipe
operations.description: A tealbrick.recipe/1 the owner imports and applies in Portal: create the agent, set it Bound with the workflow's allowed operations, connect it to each app.

operations.title: Schedule a workflow
operations.description: Create or change the schedule of a workflow for one agent (cron, 5 fields, UTC). targetMode "bound" (the default) is a Bound agent that holds the recipe of the workflow. targetMode "free" is an existing Free agent from the agent list: it claims its runs with its own access, no recipe is applied, so policyVersion must be left out (422 policy_version_not_applicable) and the agent must be a Free agent of this workspace (422 agent_not_free). An edit without targetMode keeps the stored mode. Each run becomes a Task Board issue in kanbanProject: a project you share with the agent in Task Board, so the agent can read and comment on its runs. When Task Board is connected, a new schedule needs kanbanProject (kanban_project_required); an edit can keep an old schedule without one but not remove one.

operations.title: Pause or resume a schedule
operations.description: Pause (no new runs) or resume a schedule.

operations.title: Delete a schedule
operations.description: Delete a schedule. Its run history stays.

operations.title: Schedules
operations.description: All schedules (targetMode: bound or free) with their next due time and warnings (a version that needs a new recipe; no Task Board project). kanbanLinked: Evolving Workflows can reach Task Board.

operations.title: Run history
operations.description: Runs of one schedule or of all schedules, newest first. policy_stale: the due run was not offered because the active version needs a new recipe.

operations.title: Workflow cycles
operations.description: The cycle ledger: one cycle per workflow version, from its promotion until the next version is promoted. Run counts, ratios and the live eval (gates: no duplicate claim, uncertain at most 5%, completed at least 80%, no drop over 10 points from the previous version). Newest promotion first, at most 500. Each cycle carries runMetrics: what the runners reported with routine_report metrics (runs with metrics, ok ratio, median and mean minutes, total retries, total questions to the owner, lesson count, and namedMetrics: each named per-pipeline number with its report count, median, mean, min and max), to compare versions. declaredMetrics lists the metric names that the pipeline contract of the version declares, in contract order (null when the version was not imported).

operations.title: One workflow cycle
operations.description: One cycle (workflow version) with its live eval and its stored evals, newest first (at most 50), its runMetrics, and the lessons the runners reported for this version (owner only; free text written by agents; newest first, at most 500).

operations.title: Store a cycle eval
operations.description: Store the eval of one cycle as it is now (trigger owner). Promotion of the next version stores the closing eval of the previous one by itself.

operations.title: Check a workflow contract
operations.description: Check a tealbrick.workflow/1 contract without saving it. Give the contract, or workflowId and version of a saved one. It lists every error and warning (refs that do not resolve, type clashes between steps, unbounded loops, operations that are not agent operations of an installed app, operations without idempotency, unknown model roles). When it is valid it also lists the operations the workflow would use. Owner only.

operations.title: Save a workflow contract version
operations.description: Check and save a contract as an immutable version (workflow id and version come from the contract). A saved version never changes: edit it as the next version. Saving does not run or activate anything. Owner only.

operations.title: Contract versions
operations.description: All saved contract versions with their activation state (active, superseded, deactivated or not activated). Owner only.

operations.title: Get a contract version
operations.description: Read one saved contract version and its activation. Owner only.

operations.title: Activate a workflow version
operations.description: Activate a saved version. The answer lists every operation, CRUD action, scope type and tool the version uses. The engine refuses any other call of this workflow (not_in_workflow). The bridge limits Evolving Workflows as a whole; each workflow's own limit is enforced by the engine until per-workflow grants. A newer version replaces the active one; runs already started may finish. Owner only. Schedules that follow the active version are checked again against the new version; one that no longer fits is paused and listed in staleSchedules with the reason. A workflow step that starts another workflow needs that workflow to be active; its operations are listed with via.

operations.title: Deactivate a workflow
operations.description: Stop a workflow: the engine refuses every call of all its versions, and its schedules are paused. Runs in flight fail at their next call. Owner only.

operations.title: Set a workflow schedule
operations.description: Create or change a Temporal schedule of an activated workflow. Give cron (five fields) or every (15m, 6h, 1d), and an IANA time zone. Overlap is skip by default and the catch-up window is one hour. kind poll uses the poll trigger of the contract: the run stops early when the cursor did not change. Owner only.

operations.title: Pause or resume a workflow schedule
operations.description: Pause (no new runs) or resume a Temporal schedule. Owner only.

operations.title: Run a workflow schedule now
operations.description: Start one run of a schedule at once and return its run id. Each request starts its own run, whatever else is running; the same request sent again (same idempotency key) returns the same run. Owner only.

operations.title: Delete a workflow schedule
operations.description: Delete a Temporal schedule. Its run history stays. Owner only.

operations.title: Workflow schedules
operations.description: All workflow schedules with their Temporal state, next run and last run. Owner only.

operations.title: Workflow runs
operations.description: Runs of the engine, newest first (status, timing, steps done and failed, held waits, model tokens). It holds no data of other apps. Owner only.

operations.title: Workflow run
operations.description: One run with its step timeline (attempts, held waits, sizes, error codes) and, when it finished, its outputs. Owner only. The workflow id is optional: a run id is unique in practice. Each step also carries input, output and error when Temporal still has the history (owner only; app.db keeps sizes, not bodies).

status.description: running, completed, failed, skipped, waiting_hold, waiting_agent or waiting_owner

errorMessage.description: A short reason the owner may read: the Rules denial text (200 characters at most) of a hook_denied step, or the reason code of an agent step that could not be offered. Null otherwise.

ruleId.description: The Rules rule that denied the call (rul_<ULID>), when the denial names it.

operations.title: Run a workflow now
operations.description: Start one run of an activated workflow now (a manual trigger). Give the inputs the workflow declares; the run uses the active version unless you name another activated version. Owner only.

companions.purpose: Spots repeated done work, records each scheduled run as an issue, and lets approved workflow steps read and write Task Board work.
Approved workflow steps read the knowledge base and may add notes or documents.
Approval steps ask the owner in Inbox and read the answer. Nothing else in Inbox changes.
Approved workflow steps may read why a rule decided and may propose a rule draft for the owner.
Approved workflow steps read connected services (mail, calendars, data) and call the tools the owner approved.
Lets a workflow wait for the owner to decide a held call: it reads which holds are still pending. Read only.

modelRoles.help: Used by workflow steps that write or decide (ai step with by role reasoning).
Used by workflow steps that classify or extract (ai step with by role utility).
Used by workflow steps that summarise (ai step with by role summarize).
Used by workflow steps that need a long, free-form pass (ai step with by role dreaming).
